KICD core competencies for this sub-strand:
• Learning to learn: the learner discusses in a group and generates the laws of indices.
• Digital literacy: the learner reads and obtains common logarithms of numbers from tables and calculators.

Additional competencies developed in this sequence (not in the KICD design for this sub-strand):
• Critical Thinking and Problem Solving: the learner derives laws of indices and applies logarithmic methods to solve multi-step computations such as working out the cost per kilogram of maize bought in bulk by a Rift Valley farmer, selecting the most efficient computational strategy.
• Communication and Collaboration: the learner discusses and explains index laws and logarithmic procedures with peers during group activities, clearly articulating mathematical reasoning using correct notation.
• Digital Literacy: the learner uses scientific calculators and, where available, digital devices to determine common logarithms and antilogarithms, comparing results with mathematical tables to build confidence in both tools.
• Learning to Learn: the learner independently reads logarithm tables, identifies patterns in the laws of indices, and applies acquired strategies to unfamiliar numerical problems encountered in daily Kenyan contexts.

records.old: Part A — Formal Definition (10 min). The teacher writes on the board: 'log₁₀ x = n  ↔  10ⁿ = x' and reads it aloud twice. Learners copy this into their notes with a box around it. Learners then individually complete a six-item rapid conversion table (exponential → log form and log → exponential form) on their worksheet. Part B — Characteristic and Mantissa (12 min). Teacher introduces the decomposition: any common logarithm = characteristic (integer part, can be negative) + mantissa (decimal part, always 0 ≤ mantissa < 1). Using the examples log₁₀ 3,500 ≈ 3.5441: characteristic = 3 (because 1,000 ≤ 3,500 < 10,000, i.e., 10³ ≤ 3,500 < 10⁴), mantissa = 0.5441 (read from table). value.criterion: Use of index laws and notation
value.excellent: Exceeds Expectations: Correctly states and applies the product, quotient, zero, power, negative and fractional index laws with the tea-farm data, and explains why each law works by expanding repeated multiplication.
value.proficient: Meets Expectations: Applies most index laws correctly to the tea-farm numbers, with brief or partial explanation of why they work.
value.developing: Approaches Expectations: States some laws but makes errors in applying them, or gives answers without reasons or without reference to the tea farm.

value.excellent: Exceeds Expectations: Defines the common logarithm as an exponent of 10, correctly identifies characteristic and mantissa, and accurately describes the four-step antilog procedure and why the antilog is the inverse of the log.
value.proficient: Meets Expectations: Gives the definition and handles characteristic and mantissa correctly, with minor gaps in explaining the antilog procedure.
value.developing: Approaches Expectations: Confuses logarithms with ordinary numbers, or cannot separate characteristic from mantissa, or cannot describe how the antilog works.

value.criterion: Explaining why log laws work and using them in calculations
value.excellent: Exceeds Expectations: Derives the product, quotient and power laws from the index laws, completes the calculations accurately with every step and law named, and the answers match the model values to the accuracy of the four-figure tables.
value.proficient: Meets Expectations: Completes the calculations with mostly correct steps and answers, with the derivation of the log laws partly explained.
value.developing: Approaches Expectations: Calculation steps are missing or incorrect, or the log laws are stated without any connection to the index laws.

value.criterion: Answering the driving question with Kenyan context
value.excellent: Exceeds Expectations: Gives a coherent, connected final answer that links index notation, the log laws and the four-figure tables, and uses the Kericho tea-farm data and at least one other Kenyan context accurately.
value.proficient: Meets Expectations: Gives a clear answer that uses the tea-farm data and at least one index law and one log law, with some connections missing.
value.developing: Approaches Expectations: Gives a general or incomplete answer that does not use the tea-farm data or fails to link indices to logarithms.
